headline: The warehouse grew a traffic law
lede: One builder slot shipped a build refusal players can feel — long tight aisles are now rejected unless they leave a passing bay — while a QA ruling from Jon was recorded where it can never be re-litigated by a kick.

notes.text: FLOOR BOSS #2614 (live): completing a 5-cell tight aisle with both mouths open and no bay is refused on screen NO PASSING LANE — money back, hash untouched; five is the shortest lane whose head-on meeting fits fully inside the walls. 190/190 gates, mutant killed by name.

ARENA ARCHERY: Jon's ruling B on #2585 shipped as law-in-README — single-row hangs declined, thick-stone hangs stand, marked DISCLAIMER so declined work can never score for a weakness kick again (#2623).

A weakest-game kick can name work that may not ship: Prince of Persia's only open gap is a check-only 'if Jon wants' item, CivV's is the Stage-1 scope-cut list, PickRush's calls itself 'not a feel task'. The never-dry stage steps down to the oldest gap that still asks for gameplay — and files the disqualification list so the step stays auditable.

Prod verification got honest: Vercel builds name their chunks differently than local builds, so prove deploys by grepping the role marker (an old law string) inside the live chunk set, with LC_ALL=C — zsh grep chokes on minified JS otherwise and silently misses.

look.text: EXCITEBIKE: the crash league — rivals fly, wipe out and remount
SMASH TV: the arcade gives no spawn invulnerability — NO MERCY (#2491)
